problem: Existing embodied VLM/VLN benchmarks are single-domain, use static sensor setups, multiple-choice or templated questions, and rarely isolate semantic/spatial/temporal/physical understanding, so high scores can reflect inductive bias and overfitting rather than generalization.
motivation: VLMs are increasingly used as unified perception-reasoning-control interfaces for autonomous systems, but it is unclear how embodiment (platform, sensor set, modality) affects their competence. A benchmark is needed that couples scenario understanding (VQA) with closed-loop control (VLN) across heterogeneous embodiments and probes generality with domain-far queries.
key_idea: Embodied4C is a closed-loop, exam-style benchmark with ~1.1K handcrafted free-form VQA questions and 58 one-shot VLN tasks over driving (CARLA), aerial (AirSim) and manipulation (RLBench), scored by a GPT-5 judge, to attribute embodied competence to semantic, spatial, temporal and physical reasoning.
insight: The results show that scale is not decisive: GPT-5-mini (39.59) beats GPT-5 (36.00), and the VLA models score near zero because their language and action pathways do not transfer beyond their training domains. Spatial and temporal sub-capabilities (e.g., distance estimation, mean 7.46) are the consistent bottleneck and directly degrade VLN, while semantic/physical reasoning and domain-far generality are near saturation for the strongest models. PCA (PC1 72.4%, PC2 17.7%) confirms the separation between generalist VLMs and specialized VLAs.
method: Benchmark structure: 1,149 handcrafted non-templated VQA pairs (driving 383+54 domain-far, aerial 358+41, manipulation 408+30) and 58 VLN tasks (16 driving, 22 aerial, 20 manipulation), with 13 sensor setups and 18 VQA subcategories.

Embodiment domains: CARLA driving (5 vehicle sensor stacks), AirSim UAV (5 environments, varied cameras/weather), RLBench manipulation (Franka Panda, Sawyer, UR5), with a unified system prompt plus domain-specific JSON/array action-space prompts.

VQA protocol: a reference agent drives each scenario so that all models see identical observations; free-form answers scored 0-100 by a GPT-5 judge, numeric answers by a relative-deviation formula; averaged over capabilities.

VLN protocol: single-attempt tasks with binary 0/100 or graded scoring (max 50 for partial distance progress, 100 when the target condition holds); safety termination (collision, lane invasion, red light) and timeouts excluding inference latency.
Score aggregation: S_b = mean(VQA, VLN) per embodiment, E4C-S = mean over three embodiments, plus a separate generality (GEN) score from domain-far questions.
Diagnostics: atomic logs per item, sub-capability heatmaps, coefficient-of-variation analysis and PCA of model capability profiles.

setting.backbone: 10 pretrained VLMs evaluated as-is (FastVLM-0.5B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Gemma3-4B-IT, LLaMA 4 Maverick, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o, GPT-5-nano/mini/5) plus 4 VLA/domain models (Senna, OpenFly-Agent, OpenVLA, MolmoAct); GPT-5 as judge
setting.training_data: none (benchmark; models evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning)
setting.observation: multi-view RGB with optional depth/fisheye/LiDAR/radar/HD map/GNSS-IMU (driving); RGB+depth plus telemetry (UAV); simulated manipulation camera views
setting.action_space: CARLA JSON control (throttle/brake/steer/lights); AirSim velocity vx,vy,vz,duration,yaw_rate; RLBench 7 joint positions + gripper
setting.privileged: none for agents (reference agent navigates VQA scenarios; judge sees ground truth)

numbers.extra: one-shot single-attempt, GPT-5 judge; best overall

numbers_note: This is a benchmark paper; only the evaluated models' scores are given, not a proposed method. Only the best-scoring model is listed, plus its per-embodiment scores. The full table has 14 models.
results: GPT-5-mini achieves the highest E4C-S (39.59), followed by GPT-5 (36.00), while Claude and LLaMA 4 fall at 28-32 and VLA models (Senna, OpenFly-Agent, OpenVLA, MolmoAct) score near zero (0.31-8.33). VQA is easier than VLN for all generalist models, and spatial/temporal reasoning remains the main bottleneck.
limitations: Small VLN set (58 one-shot tasks) with single-attempt scoring gives noisy estimates, and the results rely on a GPT-5 judge that may bias scoring toward the GPT family.
Simulation only; the VLAs were evaluated with bypassed action heads/4-bit precision and remapped action interfaces, which may unfairly depress their scores.
Safety, latency, hallucination, multi-agent and lifelong tasks are not covered.
